stories.title: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years over 191 murders
bullet_points: Paul Mackenzie convicted over the deaths of 190 children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families  The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.

The sentence, comprised of 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa  found the cult leader guilty  of the crimes.

bullet_points: Patient is ⁠in ​stable condition and will be transferred to a specialist ‘high consequence’ infectious disease unit  A British healthcare worker with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the UK for medical treatment, it has been confirmed.
“A British citizen currently in the DR Congo has tested positive for Ebola,” a spokesperson for the UK government said in a statement on Wednesday.
“The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated … The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low.”   Continue reading...

stories.title: ANC faces anger over poor services as South Africans vote in local elections
bullet_points: Party expected to get less than a third of the vote amid frustration over water outages and power cuts  The African National Congress is on course for a bruising result in South Africa’s local elections on Wednesday as voters go to the polls amid deep discontent over water outages, power cuts and crumbling infrastructure.
The former liberation movement, which Nelson Mandela led to power in 1994 at the end of apartheid as South Africa’s first black president, is still likely to be the largest party.
However, polls showed it getting less than a third of the vote, down from 45.6% at the  last municipal elections  in 2021 and 40.2% in  2024’s national elections .

stories.title: Sinkholes, scarred land and scapegoats: the scourge of illegal gold mining in Johannesburg
bullet_points: There is no end in sight for the drivers of illegal mining, while police action appears ineffective  Cora Bailey has been encountering illegal miners ever since she first started treating injured animals in the townships around Roodepoort, west of Johannesburg, in 1991.
But as the price of gold has soared, so too has activity in the abandoned mine shafts that mark the area.

In late September, dozens of  zama zamas  – the name given to illegal miners in South Africa, meaning roughly “to take a chance” in Zulu – arrived to dig for gold across the dirt road from her charity, Claw (Community Led Animal Welfare).
